clue.text: Vehement abuse from one stuck in traffic

indicators.note: stuck in says the word for one is lodged inside the word for traffic

parts.note: to traffic is to trade, especially illicitly
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A motorist caught in a jam lets fly with a stream of furious swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' puts I inside TRADE; 'traffic' looks like cars on a road but is the verb meaning to deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech of denunciation is exactly what vehement abuse describes.

clue.text: Actor may be the sort found thus

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: An actor might be precisely the kind of person discovered in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' reads as discovered but is the metalworking verb; 'thus' points back to the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor repeatedly given the same kind of role becomes stuck in one stereotyped part.

clue.text: Give a new form to English phrase

definitions.text: Give a new form to English phrase

indicators.note: giving the letters a new form means rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to reword an English expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a new form to' rearranges E and PHRASE, and the whole clue also defines the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To remodel something is to alter its form, to mould it again.

clue.text: Insect in slow motion over the tent-flap

parts.note: a drag is a slow, tedious movement
on means over, as in a lid on a box
the fly is the flap over a tent's entrance

explanation.surface: A bug crawls laboriously over the flap of a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' links definition and wordplay; 'slow motion' looks cinematic but gives DRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonfly is a long-bodied predatory insect with two pairs of transparent wings.

clue.text: Sailors in the drink

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; ABS is the plural
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crew of seamen have fallen overboard into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is slang for the sea, but here 'the' joins the wordplay and 'drink' alone is the definition, an aniseed spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed liqueur, a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Colossal bargaining, with Bond in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble means disturbed, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge haggling session leaves the secret agent in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges BARGAINING and BOND; the word comes from Brobdingnag, the land of giants in Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Brobdingnag is the land of giants in Swift's Gulliver's Travels, hence gigantic.

clue.text: Greek princess with short dainty foot

parts.note: Io was a princess of Argos in Greek myth, loved by Zeus

indicators.note: short says the word for dainty loses its last letter

parts.note: nice can mean dainty, fastidious

explanation.surface: A Greek princess with a small, delicate foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the E from NICE; 'foot' is the metrical unit of verse, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody an ionic is a metrical unit of two long and two short syllables.

clue.text: It. finally says where Newcastle stands in annuity scheme

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the abbreviation It.
says means what follows is spoken, so its sound is written down

parts.note: Newcastle is on the River Tyne, so it stands on Tyne

explanation.surface: Italy, at last, is said to be where a northern English city lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T from 'It.'; 'says' gives the sound of 'on Tyne' as ONTINE. Newcastle upon Tyne is a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tontine is an investment plan where subscribers share a fund and the last survivor takes all.

clue.text: What the players all do at close of play?

definitions.text: What the players all do at close of play?

parts.words: What the players all do at close of play?
parts.note: reads as athletes leaving the field, but means the stage direction for actors leaving together at a drama's end

explanation.surface: A question about what sportsmen do when the match finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction meaning 'they go out' tells actors to leave the stage.

clue.text: Christians led presumably by the Vicar-general

definitions.text: Christians led presumably by the Vicar-general

parts.words: Christians led presumably by the Vicar-general
parts.note: a vicar-general is a church official, but read as a vicar who is a general he would lead fighting believers

explanation.surface: A church official at the head of his flock.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of believers on earth struggling against evil is called the warring church in theology.

clue.text: Hard nut has one topic — reform

indicators.note: to reform is to shape anew, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tough-minded campaigner has a single cause: reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges HAS, I and TOPIC; 'Hard nut' reads as a tough person but means a nut with a hard shell.
explanation.definitionFit: The pistachio is a green-kernelled nut in a hard shell.

clue.text: Just the sort of word for the occasion

definitions.text: Just the sort of word for the occasion

parts.words: Just the sort of word for the occasion
parts.note: reads as praise for an apt remark, but describes a word coined for one single use and never again

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who found exactly the right thing to say.
explanation.definitionFit: A word invented for one particular use only is called by lexicographers a word of this kind.

clue.text: Extremely commercial affair — a racket

indicators.note: extremely picks out the extremes, the first and last letters, of commercial

parts.note: an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: A business love affair turns out to be a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives C and L, the first and last letters of 'commercial'; 'racket' suggests a swindle but means a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud continuous noise of shouting is a din or uproar.

clue.text: Word book has a line missing in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: missing says the letters for a line are lacking from the word book

parts.note: a dictionary is a book of words
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A lexicon has an entry left out, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes A and RY (railway) from DICTIONARY; 'in a manner of speaking' looks like an idiom but 'manner of speaking' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is the way a person enunciates and chooses words, their style of talk.

clue.text: Girl a fellow finds an armful

parts.note: she, the female pronoun, stands for a girl
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A young woman discovers her boyfriend is quite a handful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an armful' teases the idea of a cuddly partner; it means a bundle of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle of reaped corn stalks tied together, about as much as can be carried in the arms.

clue.text: What one gets after the opening of gin in a German house?

definitions.text: What one gets after the opening of gin in a German house?

indicators.note: in says the opening letter goes inside the name of the German house

parts.note: Hanover is a German royal house, which supplied British kings from George I

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The morning-after headache from drinking gin in a German home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the opening of' gives G, which 'in' puts inside HANOVER; the whole clue also describes the result of a night on the gin.
explanation.definitionFit: The headache and nausea that follow heavy drinking are the after-effect of too much alcohol.

clue.text: Perhaps Pan's right to go for a set of pipes

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: the letters of the word, with its s kept
taken as written

explanation.surface: The god Pan is entitled to leave in search of his pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges PANS, R and TOGO; Pan's pipes are a red herring, as 'set of pipes' means one rank of pipes on an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: On a pipe organ each knob controls a rank, a matching series of pipes.

clue.text: The vessel is holed

parts.note: suggests a ship with a breach in its hull, but describes a kitchen bowl made full of perforations on purpose

explanation.surface: A ship has been holed below the waterline.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated kitchen bowl for draining vegetables.

clue.text: Byron's descendent is like an Arab

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
a Syrian is an Arab

explanation.surface: A claim that a poet's offspring resembles a desert nomad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descendent' means one coming down: Byron's poem The Destruction of Sennacherib opens 'The Assyrian came down like the wolf on the fold'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Byron's best-known line, the ancient invader from Mesopotamia is the figure who comes down upon the fold.

clue.text: Hunter frees shark with one sound eye

indicators.note: frees means the letters are loosened and come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: sound here means spoken, the word eye heard as a letter

parts.note: the word eye, said aloud, is the letter I

explanation.surface: A hunter releases a shark that has only one good eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frees' rearranges SHARK and I; 'sound' turns 'eye' into its spoken letter I. A shikari is a big-game hunter in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Shikari is an Anglo-Indian word for a big-game huntsman or guide.

clue.text: The part of asparagus to relish

indicators.note: The part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner savours a bit of asparagus with enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment, the zest with which one tucks in.

clue.text: Remit out of American money and cease payment

indicators.note: out of here says the word for remit is outside the other pieces

parts.note: to remit money is to send it
P, penny, is a small unit of money

explanation.surface: Sending American cash abroad, then stopping payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is the container signal here, the remitted word wrapped outside; 'cease payment' is the definition, so 'Remit' is not the definition despite meaning cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt payments temporarily is to put them on hold, as a bank stops honouring cheques.

clue.text: Conceal in riddle

definitions.meaning: to hide something from view behind a partition
a riddle is a coarse sieve for grading soil or gravel

explanation.surface: Hiding the answer in a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide behind a partition, and a sieve for sorting gravel: both senses of one word.

clue.text: Church put one against wine

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
anti means opposed to, against

explanation.surface: A congregation takes a stand against drinking wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red Italian table wine from Tuscany.

clue.text: Sweetheart in French resort may have an avuncular relationship

indicators.note: in says the heart of sweet sits inside the resort name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A lover on the Riviera may be with her uncle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' is a crossword convention for E, the middle of 'sweet'; 'in' puts it inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter has an uncle, so stands in that uncle-related kinship.

clue.text: Chap outside is taking a broom

indicators.note: outside says the word for chap goes round the next word

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: A man standing outdoors picks up a broom to sweep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container signal and 'taking' adds the A at the end; 'broom' is the shrub, not the brush.
explanation.definitionFit: Genista is the botanical genus of yellow-flowered shrubs commonly called broom.

clue.text: Avoid commercial break in the evening

indicators.note: break in says the commercial interrupts, going inside the word for the evening

parts.note: eve is the evening, as in poetry
an ad is a commercial, a television advertisement

explanation.surface: A viewer dodges the advert that interrupts evening television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break in' is the container signal; 'commercial break' looks like one phrase but splits across two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or sidestep something, to dodge it.

clue.text: Segregation for some die-hard in retreat

parts.note: some of a thing is a part of it, read as a part

indicators.note: in retreat says the letters go backwards, as an army withdrawing goes back

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on a pencil

explanation.surface: Separation of groups is still upheld by some stubborn diehards as they fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns DIE and H (hard), split from 'die-hard', backwards to give HEID.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was the South African system of enforced racial separation.

clue.text: Symbol includes one plant — a kind of rose

indicators.note: includes says the word for symbol holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: a note is a written musical symbol
the Roman numeral for one is I
to set is to plant, as seeds or seedlings

explanation.surface: An emblem features a single flower, a particular rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' is the container signal; 'plant' is the verb meaning to put in the ground, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisettes are a class of climbing roses first bred in South Carolina.

clue.text: Spotted talking to the king having a rest at snooker

indicators.note: talking means the word for spotted is said aloud, giving its sound

parts.note: spotted means seen, spied
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone seen chatting to the monarch while taking a break at the snooker table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' gives the sound of SPIED, written SPIDE, then R (rex) follows; in snooker a cue rest with a raised bridge is so named.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a raised cue-rest with long legs, used to play over a ball, takes its name from the eight-legged creature.
